items.item_text: License to practice electrical engineering in the State of California.
Bachelor's degree and / or equivalent combination of experience and training in electrical engineering.
8 years of electrical engineering experience as applied to building and site infrastructure systems including planning, design, and construction of complex, new and renovation projects.

Experience with a wide range of institutional or university campus project types such as research laboratories, classrooms, lecture halls, academic and administrative offices, student housing, food service facilities, recreational facilities, campus planning and infrastructure.

Engineering experience in evaluating building and site electrical infrastructure systems, including medium voltage distribution systems and sub-stations as well as planning, design, and construction of such systems in new and renovation projects.
Knowledge and experience with the Campus Design Guidelines, policies, procedures and practices specific to capital project administration for the University of California and the Davis campus

Experience analyzing architectural and engineering drawings, equipment specifications, and installations with special emphasis on engineered systems such as electrical, fire alarm, telecommunications services, lighting, power and signal systems including skills to identify methods of improvement and develop approaches and solutions.
Knowledge and experience using AutoCAD program in developing design drawings and details and skills to collect, analyze, and summarize data into report form; and incorporate text, charts.

Under the direction of the Associate Director of Engineering - Engineering & Commissioning (AD-E&C), the Campus Engineer, and in high level coordination with the University Architect, the Electrical Engineer (EE) is responsible for providing specialized engineering services to support the development of capital projects on the UC Davis campus. The primary job functions include design and submittal review services, engineering and design services, infrastructure planning services, and commissioning and construction administration support. The EE performs work with a high level of independence and serves as a technical leader in their field of expertise, assisting project management teams with projects of critical importance to the organization. The EE is responsible for executing multiple review projects simultaneously. The EE is responsible for the evaluation and coordination of technical systems or other customized construction activities within the area of engineering expertise. The EE advises management and consults with industry professionals in designing, planning and implementing complex, electrical systems
30% - Utility and Coordination with Campus Programs
Written and verbal communication skills to prepare clear, concise, and professional reports and correspondence using MS Word and Excel.
Knowledge in the development and production of building and utility feasibility studies and assessments as well as complete design documents for projects.

Knowledge of architectural, engineering, and construction practices; ability to research, interpret and apply California Building Codes, National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) regulations, Uniform Fire Codes, university policies and other applicable codes and regulations.
